classification.difficultyReason: Identify the major arc and chord as the curved shape's boundary, infer the 270-degree arc, calculate the chord with Pythagoras, and combine it with the supplied arc-length formula. The trapezium also requires halving the base difference.

content.prompt: Find the perimeter of these shapes, correct to two decimal places.

spec.description: An oblique triangle with its right angle at the upper vertex. The long leg rises from the lower left; the short leg descends to the right.
spec.mathematics: Perpendicular legs measure 18 cm and 10 cm. The opposite hypotenuse is unlabelled.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given lengths and right-angle marker are visible.

spec.description: An unfilled isosceles trapezium with horizontal bases, matching double ticks on the sloping sides, and an external vertical height dimension.
spec.mathematics: Bases measure 6 mm and 8 mm; perpendicular height is 4 mm. Each sloping side has horizontal displacement (8−6)/2=1 mm.
spec.answerVisibility: Given dimensions and equality ticks are visible; auxiliary triangles and calculated lengths are solution-only.

answer.short: $22.25\text{ mm}$. Each sloping side is $\sqrt{17}\text{ mm}$.
answer.worked:
The equal sloping sides give equal horizontal offsets. Let $s$ be one sloping side.
$$\begin{aligned}d&=\frac{8-6}{2}\\&=1\text{ mm}\\s&=\sqrt{4^2+1^2}\\&=\sqrt{17}\text{ mm}\\P&=6+8+2\sqrt{17}\\&\approx22.25\text{ mm}\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: An unfilled circular segment bounded by a 270-degree major arc and the chord from the leftmost point to the bottommost point. Dashed black radii meet at a marked centre.
spec.mathematics: Both radii are 2 m, have matching ticks, and meet at 90 degrees. The perimeter consists of the major arc and a chord of length √8 m.
spec.answerVisibility: The radius label, centre, construction radii, equality ticks and right-angle marker are visible. Calculated chord and arc lengths are hidden.

answer.short: $12.25\text{ m}$. Add the $270^\circ$ arc and the chord.
answer.worked:
The major arc has angle $360^\circ-90^\circ=270^\circ$. Let $c$ be the chord.
$$\begin{aligned}c&=\sqrt{2^2+2^2}\\&=\sqrt8\text{ m}\\l&=\frac{270}{360}\times2\pi\times2\\&=3\pi\text{ m}\\P&=3\pi+\sqrt8\\&\approx12.25\text{ m}\end{aligned}$$
